_meta.title: GridWise LLM - exhaustive local test pack
_meta.event: BUP CSE Fest 2026 Hackathon - Online Preliminary
how_to_use: POST each case.input object to POST /optimize-energy.
Compare directive_interpretation exactly on note_index, applies, directive_type, hours and numeric values. The free-text explanation is NOT compared.

Replay the returned hourly_plan against the expected directives: energy balance, effective solar, battery bounds and rate limits, reserve floors, charge/discharge bans, grid caps, end-of-day neutrality.
Compare total_cost_bdt against expected_output.total_cost_bdt within 0.01 BDT.
Recompute total_grid_kwh, total_cost_bdt and peak_grid_kwh from the returned hourly_plan and confirm they match what the service reported.
For cases with raw_body instead of input, POST the raw string and assert the status code is one of expectations.http_status.
_meta.equivalence_note: reference_hourly_plan is ONE valid optimal schedule. Any other schedule is accepted when it satisfies the same directive ground truth and all GridWise rules and reaches the same total_cost_bdt within tolerance.
_meta.cost_verification: Every asserted total_cost_bdt was produced by the HiGHS dual-simplex LP and independently reproduced by a second LP with a different variable layout solved with the interior-point method; the two agree to within 0.02 BDT on every scored case. Every reference plan also passes a full judge-equivalent replay.
_meta.free_tier_note: There are more scored cases here than a free Gemini key allows in one minute (the cap is 20 requests/minute per model). Pace the run or test one category at a time, otherwise you are measuring your rate limit rather than your service.
